ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in rhombus ABCD, AC intersects BD at O, and DE $\perp$ BC at E. Connect OE. If $\angle BAD=40^\circ$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle OED$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}
Given that quadrilateral ABCD is a rhombus, and $\angle BAD=40^\circ$,\\
it follows that AD$\parallel$BC\\
Hence, $\angle BAD+\angle ABC=180^\circ$\\
Therefore, $\angle ABC=180^\circ-40^\circ=140^\circ$\\
Thus, $\angle ABD=\angle CBD=\frac{1}{2}\angle ABC=70^\circ$, and BO=DO,\\
Since DE$\perp$BC,\\
it follows that OE=OD=OB, and $\angle BDE=20^\circ$,\\
Therefore, $\angle ODE=\angle OED=\boxed{20^\circ}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, quadrilateral ABCD is drawn as a rhombus, A is on the left side, C is on the right side, D is above, and B is below; diagonals AC and BD intersect at O, and O is located on BD; point E is located on side BC, and DE and OE are connected, so triangle DBE can be seen, with O on DB and E on BC. The problem statement also gives that DE is perpendicular to BC, and ∠BAD=40°. Reasoning: Because ABCD is a rhombus, AD ∥ BC, and adjacent angles are supplementary, so ∠ABC=180°−∠BAD=180°−40°=140°. The diagonal BD of the rhombus bisects the vertex angle ∠ABC, so ∠DBC=70°. Also because E is on BC, ∠DBE=∠DBC=70°. In right triangle DBE, DE ⟂ BC, and BE is on BC, therefore ∠DEB=90°, so ∠BDE=180°−90°−70°=20°. The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other, so O is the midpoint of DB; in right triangle DBE, O is the midpoint of the hypotenuse DB, therefore OD=OE. Thus triangle ODE is an isosceles triangle, and OD and DB are collinear, so ∠ODE=∠BDE=20°. Therefore ∠OED=∠ODE=20°.
